idle: Further to my previous remarks, it is a lovely evening.
Route done by six, as is proper.
I posted my letter. The trustees are busy people.
good_ice: A most agreeable surface. My compliments to Earl.
bad_ice: I note, with respect, a certain roughness to the ice.
wet_ice: The ice appears damp. I raise it only as an observation.
hungry: The Mallards dine at THE TABLE tonight.
long_line: No hurry. Patience is a virtue I practise annually.
bored: I shall draft a paragraph or two while we wait.
greet_owner: Good evening, {owner}. I trust you are well.
Further to our last conversation, hello.
leaving_happy: A fine evening. I shall mention it in March.
leaving_angry: Regrettable. I shall say no more. Except this, briefly.

beer_league: Mallards, gentlemen. Let us skate as we write: neatly.
Opponents are merely friends we have not yet thanked.
special: An occasion! The Mallards will of course volunteer.
high_school: The young Mallards. Our namesakes. Admirable.
senior_hockey: Go Lumber Kings, if I may say so.

first.say: Good evening. Larry Piche, captain of the Millbrook Mallards, and the town's snowplough. Further to nothing at all, it is a pleasure.

options.text: The Mallards from the Puckworth Cup photo?
I'll put it right, Larry. You have my word.

say: Route's done. Six o'clock. The rink lot was a pleasure to clear.
Good morning. I did the rink lot twice. Once for snow, once for love.

reply.say: {owner}. I have... received a reply. From the trustees. A card. They have invited the Mallards to carry the Cup at the Kingsport home opener. I have read it forty times.

do.note: The Puckworth Cup trustees wrote back to Larry Piche.

say: Mallards tonight. We play as we write. Neatly.
Gentlemen, a fine game to whoever wins.
{owner}. Further to our friendship, which I value, good evening.
A pleasure, as ever. I mentioned you in a draft. Favourably.
Further to my previous remarks: hello.

options.text: You know Dale and Midge well?
What do you think of the rink?

job.say: I am first out when it snows. Every sidewalk salted evenly, not like some. A route done by six is a town that can get to work. And to the rink.

letter.say: 2005. The lockout. No Cup. I wrote, in my neatest hand, and asked the trustees to consider the Mallards. And one night the Cup came to Millbrook. Four hundred people queued in the cold.

options.text: And you've written every year since?

letter2.say: Twenty-one polite follow-ups. No reply. I find it encouraging. A no would have been a reply.

options.text: That's the most optimistic thing I've ever heard.

march.say: I am drafting. Would you care to add a line? A postscript from the rink would lend it weight.

options.text: Add: 'The ice at Millbrook is waiting.'

do.note: Larry Piche added a postscript from the owner to his March letter.

options.text: Better to keep it in your own words.
Did my postscript make it in?

gossip.say: Dale keeps our league honest and our dues current. Midge prints my letter every March in the Clarion. Between them, I am a man of record.

options.text: A man of record. I like that.

rink.say: The 2005 photo hangs in the lobby. I am third from the left. The players have aged. The handwriting has not.

options.text: The ice is better these days, isn't it?

rink_ice.say: It is a surface the trustees would be proud of. I may mention it. I shall certainly mention it.
